title: ECI affidavit on SIR is ‘deceitful and duplicitous’: Congress
shows: The Hindu reports the Congress's answer to the Election Commission's affidavit of 26 October 2026 in the Supreme Court. Jairam Ramesh, the party's general secretary for communications, called the 248-page counter-affidavit deceptive, deceitful and duplicitous. He said the Commission had first claimed the Supreme Court upheld the declaration attached to Form 6 and now says the declaration is separate and Form 6 was not amended, while an online Form 6 could not be submitted without it. He also said the two Election Commissioners had recorded objections that were disregarded and that ECINet was used to override electoral registration officers. Party president Mallikarjun Kharge posted a graphic of alleged irregularities from 12 states and one union territory and asked why the Prime Minister and the Home Minister were protecting the Chief Election Commissioner. By The Hindu's account the Commission has said its SIR orders were issued under Article 324 and the law governing it.
quote: Mr. Ramesh alleged that the Commission had engaged in “patent deception and word games” over Form 6, which is used for voter registration.
note: Read in full with Firecrawl on 28 October 2026. Published 27 October 2026, 8:46 pm IST, updated 8:47 pm, by The Hindu Bureau, New Delhi. The page shows no paywall marker. Every claim in the summary is the Congress's or The Hindu's. The report quotes Ramesh's Hindi post on X of 27 October and Kharge's post of the same day. The figures in Kharge's graphic (among them 2.07 crore left off Maharashtra's draft, 47.5 lakh in Delhi and 68.12 lakh in Gujarat) are as The Hindu lists them and were not checked against the site's tables here. The affidavit is court-52 in disputes_research/courts.json, and the hearing of 27 October is court-53.

title: Pawan Khera on the Commission's affidavit and Instagram
shows: Pawan Khera of the Congress says the Commission's affidavit is riddled with inconsistencies and contradictions, and alleges that the government asked Meta to have copies of the affidavit and explanations of it taken down from Instagram. He names no post. Earlier the same day LiveLaw reported that Instagram had blocked for users in India its reel explaining the Commission's affidavit, with the message "We received a legal request to restrict this content". At 10:21 pm IST LiveLaw said Instagram had restored the video. Neither LiveLaw nor Instagram said who made the request. No statement from Meta, the government or the Commission on the request was found.
quote: So much so that the government has now turned to its friends at Meta to get copies of the affidavit and its explanations taken down from Instagram
note: Read in full with Firecrawl on 28 October 2026. Posted 27 October 2026 at 16:03 UTC (9:33 pm IST). That the government asked Meta is Khera's allegation only. LiveLaw's post on X of 27 October at 10:39 UTC (4:09 pm IST, https://x.com/LiveLawIndia/status/2115030567712682245) reported the restriction and its update at 16:51 UTC (10:21 pm IST) said the video was restored. LiveLaw's report of the same day says Instagram blocked the reel for Indian users, and The Siasat Daily and The India Cable reported it from LiveLaw's post. A search on 28 October found no statement from Meta, the government or the Commission about the request.
